6.w: Come, hap-py souls, ap-proach your God With new me-lo-dious songs! Come, ten-der to Al-might-y grace The tri-bute of your tongues!

39.w: Je-sus, Thy bless-ings are not few, Nor is Thy Gos-pel weak; Thy grace can melt the stub-born Jew, And * bow the haugh-ty Greek.

44.w: Lord, at Thy sa-cred feet, With joy would we ap-pear; With-in Thy ear-thly tem-ple meet, To see Thy glo-ry here.

63.w: On Ju-dah's plains as shep-herds sat, Watch-ing their flocks by night, The an-gel of the Lord ap-peared, Clad * in ce-les-tial light.

112.w: Come, Ho-ly Spir-it, heav'n-ly Dove, With all Thy quick-'ning pow'rs; Kin-dle a flame of sa-cred love In * these cold hearts of ours.

119.w: Bes-tow, dear Lord, u-pon our youth, The gift of sav-ing grace; And let the seed of sa-cred truth Fall in a fruit-ful place.

129.w: My soul, be on thy guard, Ten thou-sand foes a-rise, And hosts of sins are pres-sing hard, To draw thee from the skies.

130.w: Ap-proach, my soul, the mer-cy seat, Where Je-sus an-swers prayer; There hum-bly fall be-fore His feet, For none can per-ish there.

166.w: Ye sin-ners fear the Lord, While yet 'tis called to-day; Soon will the aw-ful voice of death Com-mand your souls a-way.

167.w: If Paul in Cae-sar's court must stand, He need not fear the sea; Se-cured from harm on ev-'ry hand By * the di-vine de-cree.

205.w: And must this bod-y die? This mor-tal frame de-cay? And must these ac-tive limbs of mine Lie mould-'ring in the clay?

209.w: Thy life I read, my dea-rest Lord, With trans-port all di-vine; Thine im-age trace in ev-'ry word, Thy * love in ev-'ry line.

244.w: Come, Thou Fount of ev-'ry bless-ing, Tune my heart to sing Thy grace; Streams of mer-cy nev-er ceas-ing, Call for songs of lou-dest praise: Teach me * some me-lo-dious son-* net, Sung by * flam-ing tongues a-bove; Praise the mount I'm fixed u-pon it Mount of Thy re-deem-ing love.

303.w: Have mer-cy, Lord, on me, As Thou wert ev-er kind; Let me, op-press'd with loads of guilt, The want-ed par-don find.

348.w: And let our bod-ies part, To dif-f'rent climes re-pair; In-sep-a-ra-bly joined in heart, The friends of Je-sus are.

367.w: Vain man, thy fond pur-suits for-bear; Re-pent! thy end is nigh; Death at the far-thest can't be far; O * think be-fore Thou die!

371.w: Lord, I ap-proach Thy mer-cy-seat, Where Thou dost an-swer prayer; There hum-bly fall be-fore Thy feet, For none can per-ish there.

398.w: Oh! where shall rest be found, Rest for the wea-ry soul? 'twere vain the o-cean depths to sound, Or pierce to ei-ther pole.
